benchmark_quality.important_note: Qwen-authored tasks contain substantially more prompt/example/test/reference conflicts. Cross-eval scoring therefore follows the explicit written specification first and documents contradictions rather than blindly scoring against faulty examples.

interpretation: The Cross-Evaluation shows a smaller observed directional score gap than Phase 1, but the two phases use different task sets and aggregation contexts, so this should not be interpreted as a directly comparable reduction in intrinsic model capability.
The result is not a clean estimate of pure model difference because the two Cross-Eval directions use different task sets authored by the opposing systems.
The benchmark-authoring audit is itself an important result: question quality differs substantially by authoring set.
No universal model-accuracy claim should be made from these small benchmark sets.
